m: Om. I meditate on Bhavani as I myself, red, her eyes wavy with compassion, her hands holding the noose, the goad, arrows, and a bow, surrounded by the rays of the powers beginning with anima.
Om. The seer said:
When the daitya Chanda had been slain, and Munda had been struck down, and many armies had been destroyed, the lord of the asuras,
Shumbha, the powerful, his mind then subject to anger, ordered the preparation of all the armies of the daityas.
Today let the eighty-six daityas go forth with all their forces, weapons raised, and the eighty-four Kambus, surrounded by their own forces.
Let the fifty families of asuras whose valour is a crore, and the hundred families of the Dhaumras, go forth by my command.
Let the Kalakas, the Daurhridas, the Mauryas, and the Kalikeyas, asuras, go forth ready for battle, quickly, by my command.
Having ordered them in this way, Shumbha, lord of the asuras, of terrible command, went forth surrounded by many thousands of great armies.
Seeing that exceedingly terrible army coming, Chandika filled the space of earth and sky with the sounds of her bowstring.
Then the lion made an exceedingly great roar, O king, and Ambika swelled those roars with the sound of her bell.
Kali, her mouth stretched wide, surpassed with dreadful roars the directions, whose mouths were filled with the sounds of bow, bowstring, lion, and bell.
Hearing that roar, the daitya armies surrounded the Goddess, the lion, and Kali on all four sides, enraged.
At this moment, O king, for the destruction of the enemies of the gods and for the welfare of the lions of the immortals, endowed with exceeding valour and strength,
the powers of Brahma, Ishvara, Guha, and Vishnu, and of Indra, came forth from their bodies and went to Chandika in those same forms.
Whatever a god's form was, and however his ornament and mount, in that very way his power came to fight the asuras.
In front of a chariot yoked with swans, with a rosary and a water-pot, Brahma's power came. She is called Brahmani.
Maheshvari came mounted on a bull, bearing the excellent trident, with a great serpent as a bracelet, adorned with a streak of the moon.
Kaumari, a spear in her hand and the excellent peacock as her mount, Ambika in the form of Guha, came to fight the daityas.
Likewise Vaishnavi's power, standing upon Garuda, came with conch, discus, mace, sharnga bow, and sword in her hands.
The power of Hari, who bore the unequalled form of the sacrificial boar, also came there, bearing the body of Varahi.
Narasimhi, bearing a body like that of the man-lion, arrived there, a mass of stars thrown about by the tossing of her mane.
Aindri too, a thunderbolt in her hand, standing upon the king of elephants, arrived, thousand-eyed, just as Shakra is.
Then Chandika said to Ishana, who was surrounded by these powers of the gods, Let the asuras be slain quickly, for my pleasure.
Then from the Goddess's body came forth an exceedingly terrible, exceedingly fierce power of Chandika, roaring with a hundred jackals.
She, the unconquered, said to Ishana, whose matted hair is the colour of smoke, Go, blessed one, as a messenger to the side of Shumbha and Nishumbha.
Tell Shumbha and Nishumbha, the two exceedingly proud danavas, and the other danavas who have assembled there for battle:
Let Indra obtain the three worlds. Let the gods be the enjoyers of the offerings. You, go to the nether world, if you wish to live.
But if, from the arrogance of strength, you desire battle, then come. Let my jackals be satisfied with your flesh.
Because Shiva himself was appointed by that Goddess as messenger, she then became famed in this world as Shivaduti.
Those great asuras too, hearing the Goddess's word as told by Sharva, went filled with indignation to where Katyayani stood.
Then, right at the front, the enemies of the immortals, their indignation swollen, rained showers of arrows, spears, and lances upon the Goddess.
She cut those arrows they had sent, and the spears, lances, and axes, as if in play, with great arrows released from her bow drawn full.
In front of her, Kali moved about, making the enemies split by the fall of her spear and crushed by her skull-club.
Brahmani made the enemies' valour struck down, their energy struck down, by the sprinkling of water from her pot, wherever she ran.
Maheshvari slew daityas with her trident, and Vaishnavi with her discus, and Kaumari, exceedingly angry, with her spear.
By the fall of Aindri's thunderbolt, daityas and danavas fell to the earth by the hundred, torn open, raining floods of blood.
Destroyed by the blow of the snout, their chests wounded by the tips of her fangs, they fell before the boar form, and they were torn by the discus.
Narasimhi moved in the battle devouring other great asuras torn by her claws, the sky of the directions filled with her roar.
Afflicted by Shivaduti's fierce loud laughs, the asuras fell to the earth, and she then devoured those who had fallen.
Seeing the angry band of mothers crushing the great asuras, the soldiers of the gods' enemies perished by various counter-measures.
Seeing the daityas intent on flight, oppressed by the band of mothers, the great asura Raktabija came forward to fight, angry.
Whenever a drop of his blood falls to the ground, a great asura of his own measure rises from the earth.
That great asura, a mace in his hand, fought Aindri's power. Then Aindri struck Raktabija with her own thunderbolt.
Struck by the thunderbolt, much blood quickly flowed from him. From it warriors rose, of his form and of his prowess.
As many drops of blood fell from his body, so many men were born, of his valour, strength, and prowess.
And those men born of the blood fought there with the mothers, equally, exceedingly fierce, very terrible with the fall of weapons.
Again, when his head was wounded by the fall of the thunderbolt, blood flowed, and from it men were born by the thousand.
Vaishnavi struck him in battle with her discus. Aindri struck that lord of asuras with her mace.
From the streams of blood of him who was split by Vaishnavi's discus, the world was filled by the thousand with great asuras of his measure.
Kaumari struck the great asura Raktabija with her spear, Varahi with her sword, and Maheshvari with her trident.
And that daitya, the great asura Raktabija, filled with anger, struck all the mothers separately with his mace.
From him, struck in many ways by spear, trident, and the rest, the flood of blood that fell to the earth produced asuras by the hundred.
By those asuras born from asura blood, the whole world was pervaded. Then the gods came to the highest fear.
Seeing those gods dejected, Chandika laughed at once and said to Kali, Chamunda, make your mouth wide.
Receive with this swift mouth the great asuras born from the fall of my weapons, the drops of Raktabija's blood.
Move in the battle devouring the great asuras born from that. In this way this daitya, his blood diminished, will go to destruction.
Devoured by you, the fierce ones will not arise, nor will others. Having said this to her, the Goddess then struck him with her spear.
Kali caught Raktabija's blood with her mouth. Then he struck Chandika there with his mace.
The fall of the mace did not cause her even a little pain. From the body of him who was struck, much blood flowed.
Wherever it was, Chamunda received it with her mouth. The great asuras who rose into her mouth from the falling of the blood,
Chamunda devoured, and she drank his blood. The Goddess, with spear, thunderbolt, arrows, swords, and lances,
struck that Raktabija, whose blood Chamunda had drunk. He fell on the surface of the earth, struck by the mass of weapons,
bloodless, O king, the great asura Raktabija. Then the gods obtained an unequalled joy, O king.
Their band of mothers, intoxicated with the pride of the blood, danced.
